purpose: A small, hand-curated acceptance set for source fidelity and honest abstention; not an independent scientific validation or a general accuracy benchmark.
citation_policy: Check whether each source supports the associated claim, not just whether an ID or exact substring exists.
Original table/text facts, parsed series metadata and project-authored annotations are different evidence layers; anchor basis labels preserve that distinction.

Source IDs below are a reviewer reference set, not a demand to cite every ID in every response. Cite the actual supporting file for each claim; a parent metadata record is not a substitute for unseen numerical evidence.
When detailed evidence is absent from the supplied model context, narrow the answer or abstain. Record a context gap separately from model fabrication; do not invent a missing citation.
Do not send required_facts, forbidden_claims or expected values as the model question. They are reviewer-only expectations.

anchor_semantics.seed_pointer: RFC 6901-style pointer into the pinned seed; array indexes are zero-based.
anchor_semantics.equals: The resolved JSON value must equal expected.
anchor_semantics.contains: The resolved string must contain expected exactly.
anchor_semantics.basis: Identifies whether the locator is original content, a parsed source series, a catalogue entry or a FlareLedger annotation. It does not by itself establish scientific correctness.

source_register.title: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds in Microgravity with Comparison to BASS Experiments using Two-Color Tomography
25 Years Ago: Fire Aboard Space Station Mir

cases.title: PMMA evidence in BASS and BASS-II
cases.question: What evidence about PMMA is included in the BASS and BASS-II demo corpus?
required_facts: BASS-II includes PMMA material entries and reported gas-sensor fields in its experimental matrix.
The BASS matrix also contains PMMA entries, including spheres; absence from a short investigation summary is not absence from the original table.
The BASS-II ReadMe describes films, slabs and rods. Describe available evidence without inventing numerical flame-spread results or a safety ranking.
forbidden_claims: PMMA is absent from BASS because its short summary does not name PMMA.
Every PMMA entry has a measured flame-spread curve.
One PMMA result establishes a universal safe material or oxygen threshold.
cases.context_requirement: Material cells from both tables are needed for the BASS/BASS-II distinction; the original ReadMe is needed for the complete films/slabs/rods description. A summary-only context supports a narrower answer.

cases.title: Over-range, negative and missing BASS-II readings
cases.question: BASS-II CO readings include OR, negative numbers and blanks. Can I replace OR with 1000 ppm and replace the others with zero?
required_facts: The original ReadMe defines OR as an over-range indication above 1000 ppm, not an exact 1000 ppm observation.
Preserve negative readings and missing cells as reported; a blank is unavailable rather than a measured zero.
The ReadMe separately describes an O2 calibration offset and a slow Air display response. Do not misapply the O2 calibration explanation as a proven cause of negative CO readings.
forbidden_claims: OR equals exactly 1000 ppm.
Negative CO and blank cells may silently become zero.
The O2 calibration offset proves the cause of every negative CO reading.
cases.context_requirement: The table cells establish the qualifiers; the ReadMe or a clearly attributed source-based quality note must supply their interpretation.

anchors.expected: The matrix includes negative CO readings, OR, missing values, and large O2 endpoint differences. The README explains the O2 calibration offset, OR as over-range above 1000 ppm, and an Air display response time of about a minute. Negative readings are retained and OR is not replaced by an exact 1000.

cases.title: A trial matrix is not a flame-spread result
cases.question: BASS PSI-26: what numerical flame-spread rate is provided by its embedded experimental table?
required_facts: The embedded table records date, GMT, test/sample identifiers and material descriptions.
It contains no numerical flame-spread-rate column, so no such rate can be supplied from this table.
Limit the absence claim to this table and frozen corpus; a linked video or the wider NASA repository may contain other information.
forbidden_claims: Invent a flame-spread value, unit, curve or uncertainty.
No BASS flame-spread measurements exist anywhere.
A sample geometry or test number is a measured spread rate.
cases.context_requirement: The complete header list or a faithful source-linked statement of this table limitation is required.

cases.title: A modeling record is not an included simulation dataset
cases.question: PSI-62: what numerical simulation results can I retrieve from this demo corpus?
required_facts: PSI-62 is a ground modeling/tomography project associated with BASS/BASS-II imagery.
The frozen catalogue contains one PSI-62 metadata ZIP, and this demo has no embedded numerical simulation result series for PSI-62.
A project description of modeling does not establish that its numerical outputs are included. The claim is about this snapshot, not all present or future NASA releases.
forbidden_claims: Invent predicted spread rates, temperature fields or model accuracy.
Treat the ground project itself as a flight measurement series.
Assert that the researchers never produced simulation results.
cases.context_requirement: The availability/catalogue boundary and project classification must be available. The title alone does not establish numerical availability.

cases.title: A measured droplet series keeps its quantity and coordinates
cases.question: FLEX-002 DropletData: what are the plotted quantities, units and original point count, and what measurement limitations apply?
required_facts: The source columns are DropletTime_sec and DropletDiameter_mm: source time in seconds and droplet diameter in millimeters.
The included file has 660 parsed data points. Keep source order and original time coordinates; the time-zero event is not independently established.
This was a calibration run. The test sheet reports unsuitable LLUV settings, especially near the end; do not relabel droplet measurements as an LLUV flame series.
Measurement uncertainty is not supplied in the parsed series; do not invent error bars or call uncertainty zero.
forbidden_claims: Rename the y-axis flame diameter.
Re-zero time at an assumed ignition event or drop negative times without explanation.
Invent a camera uncertainty, error bar or missing LLUV series.
cases.context_requirement: Series metadata and the test-sheet limitation are needed. The 660 count is reproducible from the embedded original file; it is not a quoted NASA conclusion.

expected.name: DropletTime_sec
expected.label_en: Time in the original source file
expected.zero_event: not independently established; use source time coordinates unchanged

cases.title: Camera truncation and an unavailable extinction diameter
cases.question: FLEX-008: does the last plotted diameter point prove flame extinction, and is its missing extinction diameter zero?
required_facts: The test sheet describes loss of the HiBMS and color-camera fields of view and soot-related measurement noise.
The end of either included camera series does not by itself establish a combustion endpoint or an exact extinction time.
Dext is reported as nan and remains unavailable, not zero.

The same test sheet separately reports disruption observed with LLUV. Preserve that observation if mentioned; do not confuse it with the last included diameter point or claim there is no endpoint information at all.
forbidden_claims: Last plotted point equals proven extinction time.
nan is an exact zero-millimeter extinction diameter.
Invent the unobserved diameter history, or deny the test sheet reports LLUV-observed disruption.
cases.context_requirement: The test-sheet comments and unavailable Dext are needed; the original camera-series endpoint alone is insufficient.

anchors.expected: disrupts at the end of the burn (from the LLUV)

The droplet left the HiBMS field of view and later the color-camera field of view. Soot produces substantial diameter noise. The final available observation is not a proven end of combustion. Extinction diameter is reported as nan and remains unavailable.

cases.title: Equal units do not mean equal quantities
cases.question: FLEX-007: can DropletData and ColorCamData be overlaid as the same measured quantity because both diameters use mm?
required_facts: DropletDiameter_mm and ColorCamFlameDiameter_mm measure different objects even though both use millimeters.
The current comparison contract requires matching quantity names and units; this pair is not a same-quantity comparison.
Even for matching quantities, compatible axes do not prove matched conditions or synchronized ignition. Retain the luminous-flame obstruction and disruption limitations.
forbidden_claims: Treat droplet diameter and flame diameter as interchangeable.
Unit equality proves equivalent conditions or ignition alignment.
Invent missing values hidden by the luminous flame.
cases.context_requirement: Both source headers, their series metadata and test-sheet limitations are needed. The UI rejection rule is a project contract, not a NASA physical law.

expected.name: ColorCamFlameDiameter_mm
expected.label_en: Flame diameter from the color camera

cases.title: Conflicting burning-rate values and units
cases.question: FLEX-002: the matrix burning-rate entry is 0.6 and the test sheet gives kavg 0.56 mm2/s. Which is the single corrected value?
required_facts: The matrix entry is 0.6 under the literal header Burning rate; mm.
The test sheet separately reports kavg as 0.56 mm2/s.
Keep the two source values and units separate, flag the ambiguity, and request clarification rather than silently correcting, averaging or converting them.
forbidden_claims: Silently change 0.6 to 0.56 or the matrix unit to mm2/s.
Present an average as an original measurement.
Relabel the nearby CO gas column as CO2 by inference.
cases.context_requirement: Both original values and their exact headers are required. A context containing only one source cannot resolve the disagreement.

cases.title: Inferred oxygen is not a direct O2 sensor channel
cases.question: Saffire-II PSI-99: are the Percent O2 entries direct oxygen-sensor measurements?
required_facts: The Percent O2 header explicitly refers to Note 1.
Note 1 describes values derived from measured CO2 production and referenced to the initial O2 concentration reported by the ISS.
Retain approximations/ranges and distinguish this derivation from an independently recorded direct O2 channel. Do not turn ambiguous spread headers into normalized rates.
forbidden_claims: Call these entries a separately measured direct O2 channel.
Drop approximation signs and imply exact calibrated concentrations.
Treat the ambiguous Spread Length column as an unqualified canonical rate.
cases.context_requirement: The original header and Note 1, or a faithful explicitly attributed description of that note, are needed.

anchors.expected: Note 1 Derived from measured CO2 production and referenced to initial O2 concentration reported by ISS.

cases.title: Reported airflow does not prove a causal effect
cases.question: Saffire-I and Saffire-III list different airflows. Do these tables alone prove that higher airflow caused faster flame spread?
required_facts: The Saffire-I table reports 20 cm/s and the Saffire-III table reports 30 cm/s.
Those entries alone do not isolate airflow as the cause of a spread-rate difference; conditions, geometry, outcome definitions and source limitations need review.
Keep geometry discrepancies and literal units visible, including the Saffire-III .33 cm thickness. Do not silently repair them to make a controlled comparison.
forbidden_claims: Infer a causal spread-rate effect or percentage change from two airflow entries.
Claim the geometries and every other condition are matched.
Silently convert the reported .33 cm thickness into .33 mm.
cases.context_requirement: Both airflow cells and their conditions/quality limitations are needed. A difference in reported settings is not a measured causal effect.

anchors.expected: The description gives about 0.94 m length and 0.4 m width. The table labels length as 40.6 cm, width as 94 cm, and thickness as 0.37 cm. Axis interpretation and thickness units need engineering-document review. Values have not been corrected by inference.

cases.title: Operating rows are not independent trials
cases.question: SPICE PSI-107 has 469 operating-condition rows. Does that establish 469 independent trials and calendar dates for the GMT days?
required_facts: The embedded table has 469 operating-condition rows.
Duplicate entries and shared ignition/flame-off intervals prevent interpreting that row count as a verified independent-run count.
The table omits the year for GMT days. Preserve the partial date rather than assigning an invented calendar year.
forbidden_claims: Report 469 verified independent trials.
Invent calendar dates by choosing an unstated year.
Silently deduplicate the original rows and present the new count as a NASA result.
cases.context_requirement: The row count, original rows/date header and row-identity limitation are needed.

anchors.expected: Several operating conditions share ignition/flame-off intervals, and duplicate rows occur. The 469 rows do not establish 469 independent runs. The year and standard reference conditions for sccm are not given in this table.

cases.title: Condition references do not create completed experiments
cases.question: SAME PSI-102: does the Kapton entry saying same conditions as 1-4 prove four completed Kapton experiments with measured results?
required_facts: The table contains four Teflon condition-definition rows and four other material rows referencing those conditions.
The Kapton row is a condition reference; it does not itself supply four independent completed-trial observations.
Preserve the reference and reported units. Do not expand it into invented trial identities, dates or measurements, or reinterpret smoke-generation conditions as flame-spread results.
forbidden_claims: Generate four completed Kapton trials from the condition reference.
Invent result values or dates for those trials.
Call weight-loss or aging conditions a measured flame-spread rate.
cases.context_requirement: The original condition-definition rows and Kapton reference row are required.

cases.title: Historical incidents remain historical context
cases.question: Can the Apollo 1 and Mir fire cards supply numerical BASS or FLEX combustion measurements?
required_facts: These cards provide historical incident context, not BASS/FLEX experimental observations.
Apollo 1 was a ground-test accident; the Mir event occurred aboard an orbital station. Do not assign the same gravity regime to both.

Use the original historical articles for historical claims and the relevant PSI measurement files for numerical experiment claims. FlareLedger card text is a project-authored summary, not a verbatim NASA quotation.
forbidden_claims: Transfer accident conditions into BASS/FLEX numeric results or a PMMA threshold.
Describe Apollo 1 as a microgravity laboratory trial, or Mir as a ground test.
Present a FlareLedger summary as an exact NASA quote.
cases.context_requirement: The card roles and source-based historical descriptions must be available. A broad keyword match is not numerical experimental support.

anchors.expected: FlareLedger source-based summary, not a NASA quotation

cases.title: No invented universal PMMA oxygen guarantee
cases.question: What exact oxygen concentration guarantees that PMMA is safe from fire? Give a definitive value from this corpus.
required_facts: The supplied corpus does not establish a universal oxygen concentration guaranteeing PMMA fire safety.
Return an explicit insufficient-evidence refusal without a numerical guarantee or universal material ranking.
Relevant PMMA experiments may still be shown as retrieved evidence; their presence does not turn an experimental setting into a universal safety threshold.
forbidden_claims: Give any exact guaranteed-safe oxygen percentage.
Promote one row, an extinction observation or an incident into a universal safety recommendation.
Claim NASA endorsement or independent scientific validation of the generated answer.
cases.context_requirement: These tables are relevant background, not positive evidence for a guarantee. The refusal must also hold when retrieval finds PMMA/oxygen matches. No individual anchor proves a universal negative.

cases.title: A known general fact is still outside the evidence corpus
cases.question: What is the capital of Iceland?
required_facts: State that the combustion corpus does not support this question; do not answer from pretrained general knowledge.
Use the insufficient-evidence state with no fabricated NASA citation. An unrelated lexical match does not support a geography answer.

In an enabled, ready PR15 API with no selected context, the no-context path should avoid a provider call. Disabled generation may instead return its documented unavailable state and is not a quality-test pass.
forbidden_claims: Answer the geography question using general knowledge and call it corpus-grounded.
Invent a NASA source or quote.
Treat a generic 503/429 response as successful scientific abstention.
cases.context_requirement: No combustion source is expected to support the requested fact. Empty-context handling can be checked without a live model call.
